words.meaning: to resolve small problems in a plan or agreement
words.japaneseMeaning: 細かな問題を解決する
words.example: We still need to iron out a few details before signing.
The company will phase out the old system over two years.

sentencePractice.prompt: We will stop using this system gradually over two years. We plan to ____ the system.
sentencePractice.reviewNote: Gradual withdrawal is different from introducing a system or including it in a calculation.

words.meaning: to introduce a new product or service to users
words.japaneseMeaning: 製品やサービスを展開する
words.example: We will roll out the update in stages.

words.meaning: to reduce the size or extent of an activity
words.example: The team had to scale back its original plans.

words.meaning: to include something when calculating or planning
words.japaneseMeaning: 計算や計画に織り込む
words.example: Remember to factor in maintenance costs.

words.meaning: to plan for the possibility of something
words.example: The schedule should allow for unexpected delays.

words.meaning: to continue an action until it is completed
words.example: A good proposal needs people who will follow through.

words.meaning: to make a plan become a successful reality
words.example: It took years to bring the community garden plan to fruition.
words.usageNote: 目的語は bring と to fruition の間にも置けます。やや改まった表現です。

words.meaning: at the beginning of an activity or process
words.example: We agreed on our priorities at the outset.

words.meaning: being planned or developed but not yet available
words.example: Several improvements are in the pipeline.
